audit_findings.methodological_assessment: The prior falsification of the direct-support form of OPEN_BRIDGE_001 (Campaign LFCR_001) utilized an ablation strategy (Model B) that randomized orientation independently of residue and admissibility aspects. Under the 'Whole Expression Primacy' rule, this constitutes a 'component-first' analytical decomposition that is ontologically prohibited for formal framework validation.
audit_findings.isolation_confirmation: The SIM_ORIENTATION_CLOSURE_ATTACK_001.json campaign config and the engine_2d.cpp implementation confirm that orientation (I) was treated as an isolated primitive entity that could be mutated without matched transformations in the residue (R) or epsilon (E) aspects of the RT expression.
audit_findings.impact_on_previous_falsification: While the empirical observation (orientation randomization does not degrade survival) remains valid as a model observation, its interpretation as a 'falsification' of the participatory role of orientation is now classified as methodologically incomplete. The 'decoupling' observed in LFCR_001 may be an artifact of analytical fragmentation rather than a property of the whole process.
audit_findings.validation_of_reformulation: The reformulation of OPEN_BRIDGE_001 as a 'Topological Selector' bridge (satisfied in Run 08) is more consistent with Whole Expression Primacy. It treats orientation as a boundary condition on the selection of the complete topological closure (the whole expression), rather than a modular driver of a separable stability property.

recommendations: Retain the reformulated 'Topological Selector' status (C4) for OPEN_BRIDGE_001.
Add a 'Methodological Warning' to all LFCR_001 citations in the textbook, noting the violation of Whole Expression Primacy.
Mark PO_004 (Stability arises from Principle 2.X, not orientation) as 'RECONSTRUCTED_IN_SELECTOR_FORM' rather than 'PURE_DECOUPLING'.
